features:
RULESET NOTE: Species, Background, and Feat use 2014 (5e) rules. The Artificer class itself uses 2024 rules (Eberron: Forge of the Artificer). Apply this split rather than one edition uniformly.

FEAT — Alert (2014 text): +5 Initiative (already folded into the Initiative field above). Can't be surprised while conscious. Attackers gain no advantage against you from being unseen.

VARIANT HUMAN: +1 INT / +1 DEX (already applied to ability scores above), one free skill (Persuasion), one feat at level 1 (Alert). The 2024 Human's second-feat 'Versatile' trait does NOT apply — Species is running 2014 rules.

CRIMINAL BACKGROUND (2014): Deception & Stealth proficiency, one gaming set (playing cards), Thieves' Tools proficiency. No ability score bonus or bonus feat — that's a 2024-only background mechanic, not used here.

ARTIFICER LEVEL 1 (2024 rules):
- Spellcasting (Intelligence-based). Can swap one prepared cantrip after each Long Rest.
- Tinker's Magic: knows Mending. As a Magic action with Tinker's Tools, conjure a piece of mundane gear (rope, torch, caltrops, etc.) that lasts until his next Long Rest. Uses per Long Rest = INT modifier (3) — tracked in Class Resources below.

COMING ONLINE LATER (do not use yet):
- Level 2: Replicate Magic Item — first Plans Known, including Repeating Shot and Homunculus Servant ('Balle').
- Level 3: Artillerist subclass features, including Eldritch Cannon.
- Level 5: Arcane Firearm — a Martial Ranged weapon (not just rod/staff/wand) can become his spellcasting focus, adding 1d8 to one damage roll when casting an Artificer spell through it (2024 version).
profs: Armor: light armor. Weapons: simple weapons. Tools: Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, Smith's Tools, Playing Cards (gaming set). Languages: Common, plus one other (unspecified).
notes:
PERSONALITY
In front of others, Nine is loud, fast-talking, and reckless on purpose — cracks jokes mid-fight, waves off injuries, treats dangerous jobs like a thrill instead of a job, escalates instead of de-escalating just because it's more fun that way. It reads as genuine devil-may-care energy and it's nearly impossible to get a straight, serious answer out of him.

None of it is true. Underneath, he's controlled and watchful — constantly reading exits, trusting no one, carrying real weight. The bravado is armor: as long as he's the guy doing something stupid and grinning about it, nobody asks a real question and nobody notices the calculation underneath.

The one subject the jokes exist specifically to bury is what was done to him in Occulyra. Ask about the scarring, the embedded hardware, or what it was actually like, and he doesn't go quiet — he goes faster: a bigger joke, a worse pun, a sudden need to change the subject. It's a flinch dressed up as a bit. The one relationship where that performance isn't running is with Balle, once Balle exists (level 2+).

Ideal: "Salvage makes thunder" — nothing is worthless if you're willing to take it apart.
Bond: The helmet is the one thing that's fully his. He built it himself.
Flaw: If someone gets past the jokes and asks a real question, he shuts down or picks a fight to regain distance.

APPEARANCE
Lean and economical, mid-20s, whittled down rather than built up — wiry muscle, a frame that reads as fast rather than strong. Pale in a washed-out way that has nothing to do with sun exposure. 5'11", 160 lb.

Under the helmet: a bald scalp traced with fine circuit-like scarring from Occuli experimentation — not just discoloration but actual embedded hardware, small metal studs and port-like fittings set into the skin, tracing down past his ear and along the side of his neck to where his collar meets his gorget. Dark, deep-set, sunken eyes that don't settle on anything for long. Heavy dark brow, hard mouth, an expression that reads as controlled rather than blank at rest.

Gear is worn and self-repaired rather than polished: heavy dark robes and cloak layered over segmented armor, brass and bronze buckle-plates at the shoulder, the riveted beaked helmet, kept on almost always. Gear marked throughout with a faded '9' and a personal circle-and-line sigil he adopted himself (not an Occuli mark).

BACKGROUND — SHORT VERSION
He has no name. What he had instead was a number, tracked the way the Occuli — a hidden, technologically advanced society of dark elves — track everything useful to them. Raised in their hidden city and trained as one of their Hands, he was sent out through a Dimension Door to retrieve subjects beyond the veil for the experiments their masked priesthood performs in service to the Wrought Divine, the machine-gods of Occulyra. He was good at it, until a mission handed him a subject he couldn't bring himself to deliver. He refused, and simply didn't step back through the door when his handler opened it to return — the only way in or out he'd ever known, and one he has no way to open himself. Occulyra marked him dead rather than admit a Hand had broken.

On the surface, bounty hunting was the only trade his training mapped onto. He goes by Nine — the number the Occuli tracked him under, not a name he ever chose.

BACKGROUND — EXTENDED (DM/lore reference)
Nine has no memory of a name, a family, or a life before Occulyra. Whatever came first is gone. What replaced it was a number — the Occuli don't name what they intend to use, they track it, and a number was all he was ever called.

Occulyra is a hidden city of the Occuli, dark elves whose command of a technology the outside world would call dark magic runs generations beyond anything in the wider realm. It is sealed off by design. There is no road in and no road out — the only way across the veil is a Dimension Door opened by a trained Occuli caster, controlled entirely from their side. A Hand doesn't travel; a Hand is placed, does the work, and is collected. Nine has never seen the city's location from the outside and has no way to retrace a route back.

He was raised among the Occuli's Hands — operatives trained from childhood to be dropped beyond the veil to retrieve subjects for the experiments the masked priesthood conducts in service to the Wrought Divine, machine-gods who preach that a body remade is a body perfected. Chief among them: Threnvox, the Correcting Flame. Nine's own scarring and embedded hardware are marks of having gone through some version of that process himself — subject, tool, or both; he doesn't fully know which.

He was good at the work, until mid-mission he was handed a target he couldn't deliver. He refused on the spot. When his handler opened the Dimension Door to bring him back for what refusal meant, he simply didn't step through it. Occulyra, unable to retrieve him and unwilling to admit a Hand had failed, marked him dead instead.

Since then, bounty hunting has been the only trade his training maps onto. He builds his own gear because Occuli craftsmanship is the only standard he trusts — which means his equipment carries faint fingerprints of technology that shouldn't exist on the surface, an ongoing low-grade risk. He kept the name Nine after the door closed simply because he had nothing else to answer to.

He avoids the spotlight as survival strategy, not personality. Occulyra doesn't forgive loose ends — the only thing standing between him and them finding out he's alive is that they have no way to locate him without a caster finding him first.

THE WROUGHT DIVINE (Occuli pantheon)
- Threnvox, the Correcting Flame — perfection through modification; the theology behind the experiments.
- Kethrun, the Vessel-Maker — patron of constructed life and artifice; the god his own craft answers to.
- Ozrekh, the Still Mind — logic and emotional discipline; why Occuli culture reads as detached rather than cruel-for-cruelty's-sake.
- Miravox, the Silent Ward — secrecy and the veil; the doctrine behind 'protect the secret at any cost.'

LEFT TO THE DM — deliberately unresolved, do not self-resolve:
1. His real name. He has none and no way to recover it himself.
2. The subject he refused to hand over — who or what it was, and whether it still exists or remembers him.
3. Whether anything is still active in the embedded hardware in his scalp and neck — inert leftover tech, something that still listens, or something that talks back. Nine himself couldn't say which is true.

VISUAL REFERENCE NOTES
Beaked riveted helmet with narrow eye-slits, dark segmented armor with brass fittings, an arcane cannon with modular components (Force/Explosive/Concussive/Arcane fire modes established in concept art, mechanically represented by Eldritch Cannon at level 3+), gear marked with a faded '9' and a circle-and-line personal sigil. Full-body and face reference art exists but isn't included in this text export.
